creator: Connie Loizos
title: (No AI) Where was Nvidia’s security team?
dc:creator: Connie Loizos
content: Nvidia’s security chief quietly left in August, and now that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over his relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to China, a former intelligence officer says it’s the kind of leak that runs everyday conversations, which most corporate security teams are poorly equipped to catch.

title: (No AI) Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Nvidia_Jensen_huang_03.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The [latest edition](https://www.theverge.com/column/1033943/jensen-huang-nvidia-china-spying-scandal-resignation) of our [Stepback newsletter](https://www.theverge.com/newsletters) should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a [statement from Megaspeed](https://www.reuters.com/business/megaspeed-says-alice-huang-left-company-august-2025-2026-11-15/) claiming that Alice Huang hasn't worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers.

title: (No AI) Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Photo collage of a photo of the US Capitol building coming out of a computer window.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25545717/STK481_STK432_CONGRESS_GOVERNMENT_CIVRGINIA_D.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration [need to answer to Congress](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1032231/jensen-huang-will-still-need-to-answer-to-congress-despite-his-resignation-schumer-says). Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also [sent letters](https://abcnews.com/Politics/house-senate-republicans-call-howard-lutnick-jensen-huang/story?id=138111390) to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the commit …
